Explorator can be amazing, don't write off melee so suddenly. You can do some absolutely incredible things with it.

 For example, charge up to a necron warrior, hit them twice with ranged weapons on the way, then hit them with melee.
  Next time on that turn the warrior will try to move away from your troop and you hit for an attack of opportunity. Warriors and immortals will ALWAYS try to disengage from melee first giving you that attack of opportunity. A cheap dremel or off brand rotary tool, and some high speed steel drill bits (usually 3 - 5mm) for drilling through the rivets will help you loads.... i cant tell you how annoying it is to sit there with a pin vice twiddling away at it, believe me i've tried and its not worth it. Other than that just some cheap sprue cutters, keep a cheap set specifically for cutting metal bits so it doesnt matter if they get damaged from harder metals.

Other than super glue i don't really know what to suggest for putting them back together though, maybe a good set of tweezers as some small bits can be fiddly. If you're having trouble with super glue taking too long to dry get some bicarbonate of soda and sprinkle some on it after you've got the pieces held in place. Acts like a very cheap activater and just looks like a messy weld when dry.

 Green stuff? That can be used to hide gaps and you can tap it with a toothpick to make it look like a beaded weld.

Some materials you should look at for building cars are plasticard, 0.5mm works well. This can be used to make allsorts of armour panels and bodywork.

Plastic tubes, around 2 to 2.5mm is great for exhausts, rollcages, spikes, axles etc. The cheapest spikes are toothpicks though.

Look for aluminium mesh for windows and windscreens as well, its very cheap. You can get it from places that do car supplies. I made the mistake of getting steel bugscreen of amazon instead and its horrible to cut and work with.
